newsitem.title: SPAIN: No plans yet for more Fr fr bonds - Spanish Treasury.
newsitem.headline: No plans yet for more Fr fr bonds - Spanish Treasury.

text.p: Despite a very warm welcome to Spain's 1997 debut in the euromarket, the Spanish Treasury said on Thursday it was too early to say whether it would make more French franc issues this year.

"At the moment we're happy, but I can't say if we'll do more(in this currency). In 1996 we did a lot in French francs, but we decide based on market trends," Federico Ferrer, foreign debt head at the Treasury, told Reuter.
He added that Spain is planning to issue more than 600 billion pesetas in the euro market this year.
"We'll issue a bit more than 600 billion pesetas, maybe 650/700 billion pesetas," Ferrer said.
Though this is the first Spanish issue this year in French francs, Spain in recent years has launched bonds maturing in 2004, 2006, and 2008 on the secondary market.
The four-billion franc issue, maturing on April 10, 2012, was offered earlier on Thursday with a 6.25 percent coupon and an issue price of 101.145.
Right after the launch, Joe Dreyer, global head of new issues at Paribas Capital Market in Paris, said that the bond got off to a very good start and had a good reception.
"Spain can offer a very solid yield curve in French Francs and so they enjoy a strong following," Dreyer told Reuters.
He added that the issue "was bought mainly by insurance companies but pension funds are also starting to get in".
"It's a nice pick up of 15 basis points over OAT (a combination of 6.5 pct 2011 OAT and 8.5 percent 2012 OAT) for such a good borrower as Spain," Dreyer added.
Ferrer said, "A spread of 15 basis points over is normal. It's what we paid on previous issues as well."
Dreyer estimated that 80 percent of the issue would be sold inside France, while the other 20 percent was likely to be allocated in the UK and in selective trust funds around Europe.
Of Spanish foreign debt, 20.1 percent was denominated in French francs.
The Kingdom of Spain is rated AA2 by Moody and AA by Standard and Poor's. --Tiziana Barghini, Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
